705357.t: From Proto-Hellenic *heptə́, from Proto-Indo-European *septḿ̥. Cognates include Latin septem, Sanskrit सप्त (saptá), Old Armenian եաւթն (eawtʻn), Old English seofon (English seven).

705396.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wérgon, from Proto-Indo-European *wérǵom. Cognates include Old English weorc (English work), Avestan 𐬬𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬰𐬆𐬨 (var^əzəm) (Persian وَرز (varz)), and Old Armenian գործ (gorc).

705318.t: From ἐπιφανής (epĭphănḗs, “in view”) + -ια (-ĭă), from ἐπιφαίνω (epiphaínō, “to come into view”), from ἐπί (epí, “upon”) + φαίνω (phaínō, “to shine, bring to light”).

705319.t: From ἐπι- (epi-) + -φανής (-phanḗs); compare ἐπιφαίνω (epiphaínō, “to come into view”).

705317.t: From ἐπι- (epĭ-, “upon”) + φαίνω (phaínō, “to shine, bring to light”).

705333.t: From ἐπιχαίρω (epikhaírō, “rejoice over someone”), from ἐπί (epí, “upon”) + χαίρω (khaírō, “I rejoice”).

705346.t: Present stem from the e-grade of Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ- (“to follow”).

705353.t: From earlier ϝέπος (wépos), from Proto-Hellenic *wékʷos, from Proto-Indo-European *wékʷos, from *wekʷ- (“to speak”). Cognates include Sanskrit वचस् (vácas) and Avestan 𐬬𐬀𐬗𐬀𐬵- (vacah-).

705300.t: From ἐπιτηδές (epitēdés, “for this purpose”) + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix). ἐπιτηδές is from ἐπι- (epi-, “for”) + a noun τῆδος, ταδος (têdos, tădos) of unclear further origin + the suffix -ές (-és), the adverbial neuter accusative singular of -ής (-ḗs,…

705390.t: From the root of ἔργον (érgon, “work”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agentive suffix).

705322.t: From ἐπι- (epi-, “upon”) + φέρω (phérō, “to bring, bear, carry”).

705380.t: Uhlenbeck and others consider it cognate with Sanskrit रम॑ते (rámate, “to calm down; to enjoy; to have sex with”), Lithuanian rimti (“calm down”), Gothic 𐍂𐌹𐌼𐌹𐍃 (rimis, “tranquility”), which all come from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rém-e-ti with *h₁rem- (“to…

705301.t: From ἐπιτηδεύω (epitēdeúō, “to pursue an activity, to practise a thing”) + -μα (-ma).

705356.t: Formation like δρύοψ (drŭ́ops, “woodpecker”), on an onomatopoeic basis. Parallel names exist in other languages, like Latin upupa, Persian پوپو (pôpô), Armenian հոպոպ (hopop) and Latvian pupukis.

705335.t: From ἐπιχειρέω (epĭkheiréō, “to endeavour, attempt to”) + -μα (-ma, result noun suffix).

705373.t: Probably a back-formation from the aorist form εἶπον (eîpon).

705362.t: From ἑπτά (heptá, “seven”) + -άκις (-ắkĭs, suffix for adverb of repetition).
